questions.question: Which of the following Indian playback singers received the Bharat Ratna in 2001?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lata Mangeshkar**__

__
 
• **Lata Mangeshkar** received the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in 2001.
 
• The Bharat Ratna is awarded in recognition of exceptional service or performance of the highest order in any field of human endeavor.
 
• Lata Mangeshkar is one of the most respected and celebrated playback singers in India, known for her contribution to Indian cinema and music.
 
• She has recorded songs in over a thousand Hindi films and has sung in over thirty-six regional Indian languages and foreign languages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lata Mangeshkar** was born on 28th September 1929 and began her career in 1942.
 
• She has received numerous awards and honors, including the Padma Bhushan (1969), Padma Vibhushan (1999), and Dadasaheb Phalke Award (1989).
 
• Her contribution to Indian music has left an indelible mark, making her an iconic figure in the industry.
 
• The Bharat Ratna was instituted in 1954 and is conferred by the President of India.
 
• The award does not carry any monetary grant but consists of a certificate (Sanad) signed by the President and a medallion.

questions.question: Who authored the book ‘Poverty and Un-British Rule in India’ in 1901, which was highly critical of the economic impact of British Rule?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dadabhai Naoroji**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji** authored the book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' in 1901.
 
• He was a prominent Indian nationalist leader and one of the founding members of the Indian National Congress.
 
• The book was highly critical of the economic impact of British rule in India, detailing how it led to widespread poverty and exploitation.
 
• Dadabhai Naoroji is often referred to as the "Grand Old Man of India" for his contributions to the Indian independence movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Dadabhai Naoroji was the first Indian to be elected to the British Parliament, where he served as a member from 1892 to 1895.
 
• He used his position to advocate for Indian self-governance and to expose the economic injustices of British rule.
 
• His work laid the foundation for future economic critiques of colonialism and inspired many other Indian leaders in the fight for independence.
 
• Naoroji's book remains a significant historical document, highlighting the detrimental effects of colonial policies on India's economy.

questions.question: The efforts of Malayalam poet Vallathol Narayana Menon and dancer and guru Kalyanikutty Amma brought back and gave a new life to the dance form ____________.

• Vallathol Narayana Menon was a prominent figure in Malayalam literature and played a key role in the revival of classical arts in Kerala.
 
• Kalyanikutty Amma was a renowned dancer and teacher of Mohiniyattam, contributing significantly to its development and popularity.
 
• Mohiniyattam is characterized by its graceful and elegant movements, often described as the dance of the enchantress.

• The dance form combines elements of Bharatanatyam and Kathakali, two other classical dance forms from South India.
 
• Mohiniyattam's repertoire includes various dance sequences like Cholkettu, Varnam, and Padam, each with its own unique style and rhythm.
 
• The costume for Mohiniyattam is typically white or off-white with gold borders, reflecting the traditional attire of Kerala.
 
• The dance form has a rich history and continues to be an integral part of Kerala's cultural heritage.

questions.question: The outward remittances under the Reserve Bank of India’s ____________ made a strong comeback in the first quarter of FY23 as Indians increased spending on international travel, maintenance of close relatives and gifts.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Liberalised Remittance Scheme**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The outward remittances under the Reserve Bank of India's **Liberalised Remittance Scheme** made a strong comeback in the first quarter of FY23.
 
• This increase is attributed to Indians spending more on **international travel, maintenance of close relatives, and gifts**.
 
• The Liberalised Remittance Scheme allows resident individuals to remit up to **USD 250,000 per financial year** for any permissible current or capital account transaction.
 
• It facilitates **ease of sending money abroad** for various purposes, including education, travel, and investment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS)** was introduced by the Reserve Bank of India in **2004** to facilitate the outward remittance of funds.
 
• Under the scheme, the remitted funds can be used for **various purposes** such as investment in shares, property, or for meeting expenses of overseas education, travel, medical treatment, and maintenance of relatives.
 
• The scheme has undergone several amendments to **increase the limit** and include more permissible activities.
 
• It is crucial for residents to comply with the **reporting requirements and permissible limits** set forth by the RBI under the LRS.

questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) scheme provide loans up to ________ to the non-corporate, non-farm small and micro entrepreneurs. (As of April 2023)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10 lakh**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) scheme provides loans up to **10 lakh** to non-corporate, non-farm small and micro entrepreneurs.
 
• The scheme was launched by the Government of India to promote entrepreneurship and support small businesses.
 
• Loans under PMMY are categorized into three products: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,001 to ₹5 lakh), and Tarun (₹5,00,001 to ₹10 lakh).
 
• The loans are provided by commercial banks, regional rural banks, small finance banks, microfinance institutions, and non-banking financial companies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana was launched on **8th April 2015** by the Honorable Prime Minister of India.
 
• The scheme aims to provide financial support to the unfunded segment of the Indian economy and bring them into the formal financial system.
 
• The loans provided under the PMMY scheme are collateral-free, ensuring that even small entrepreneurs can avail of the benefits without the need for significant assets.
 
• MUDRA, which stands for Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency, is responsible for developing and refinancing all Micro-Finance Institutions (MFIs) that lend to small businesses.
 
• The scheme also aims to create an inclusive, sustainable, and value-based entrepreneurial culture, particularly among marginalized sections of society.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the process of calorimetry?

options.text: Measuring the amount of compressive strength
Measuring the amount of heat energy transferred

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Measuring the amount of heat energy transferred**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Calorimetry** is the science of measuring the amount of heat.
 
• This is done by observing the temperature change in a known quantity of water or other substances.
 
• The process is crucial in various fields such as chemistry, physics, biology, and engineering to determine heat transfer in chemical reactions, physical changes, and other thermal processes.
 
• Calorimeters are the devices used to perform calorimetry, and they come in various types such as bomb calorimeters and differential scanning calorimeters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Specific Heat Capacity**: The amount of heat required to change the temperature of a unit mass of a substance by one degree Celsius.
 
• **Latent Heat**: The heat absorbed or released during a phase change of a substance without changing its temperature.
 
• **Enthalpy**: A thermodynamic quantity equivalent to the total heat content of a system, often used in the context of chemical reactions.
 
• **Thermal Equilibrium**: A state in which two objects connected by a permeable barrier have no net exchange of heat energy.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 45**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 45** of the Constitution of India mandates the provision of early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years.
 
• This Article falls under the Directive Principles of State Policy, which serve as guidelines for the framing of laws by the government.
 
• The aim is to ensure that young children receive the necessary care and education to support their development and well-being.
 
• Early childhood care and education is crucial for laying a strong foundation for a child's future learning and development.
 
• In 2002, the Right to Education Act (RTE) was enacted to make education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years, complementing the directive under Article 45.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are enshrined in Part IV of the Constitution and aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• These principles are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by any court, but they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• The government is expected to apply these principles in making laws to establish a just society in India.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a constitutional body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NITI Aayog**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **NITI Aayog** is NOT a constitutional body.
 
• NITI Aayog stands for **National Institution for Transforming India**, which was established by an executive resolution of the Government of India in 2015, replacing the Planning Commission.
 
• Unlike the other options listed, NITI Aayog is a **policy think tank** of the Government of India and does not derive its authority from the Constitution.
 
• The **Election Commission, Finance Commission, and Union Public Service Commission** are all constitutional bodies, established under various articles of the Constitution of India.
 
• These constitutional bodies have specific roles and responsibilities defined by the Constitution to ensure the smooth functioning of the democratic framework and governance in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Election Commission of India** is established under Article 324 of the Constitution and is responsible for administering election processes in India.
 
• The **Finance Commission** is established under Article 280 of the Constitution and recommends the distribution of taxes between the Union and the States.
 
• The **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)** is established under Article 315 of the Constitution and conducts examinations for recruitment to various civil services of the Government of India.
 
• **NITI Aayog** aims to foster cooperative federalism through structured support initiatives and mechanisms with the States on a continuous basis, recognizing that strong states make a strong nation.
 
• It provides relevant strategic and technical advice across the spectrum of key elements of policy to the central and state governments.

questions.question: Vitamin B1 deficiency causes which nutritional disorder that causes problems with peripheral nerves and wasting?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Beri-Beri**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Beri-Beri** is a nutritional disorder caused by a deficiency of Vitamin B1 (Thiamine).
 
• It affects the peripheral nerves and muscles, leading to symptoms such as weakness, wasting, and in severe cases, heart complications.
 
• There are two types of Beri-Beri: **Wet Beri-Beri** which affects the cardiovascular system, and **Dry Beri-Beri** which affects the nervous system.
 
• It is most commonly seen in regions where the diet consists primarily of polished white rice, which lacks thiamine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Xerophthalmia** is caused by a deficiency of Vitamin A and leads to dryness of the conjunctiva and cornea.
 
• **Pernicious Anemia** is caused by a deficiency of Vitamin B12 and affects red blood cell production.
 
• **Rickets** is caused by a deficiency of Vitamin D, calcium, or phosphate and leads to softening and weakening of bones in children.
 
• Ensuring a balanced diet with adequate vitamins and minerals is essential for preventing these nutritional disorders.

questions.question: In which type of forests are wild donkeys and camels found in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thorny forests and bushes**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Wild donkeys and camels** in India are typically found in **Thorny forests and bushes**.
 
• These regions are characterized by **arid and semi-arid climates**, which are suitable for the survival of these animals.
 
• Thorny forests and bushes are primarily located in the **northwestern parts of India**, such as Rajasthan and Gujarat.
 
• The vegetation in these areas consists of **thorny trees, shrubs, and bushes** that can withstand harsh climatic conditions.

questions.question: Which curve examines the relationship between the rate of unemployment and the rate of money wage changes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phillips curve**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Phillips curve** examines the relationship between the rate of unemployment and the rate of money wage changes.
 
• It suggests that there is an inverse relationship between the rate of unemployment and the rate of inflation in an economy.
 
• The curve was introduced by economist A.W. Phillips in 1958, based on empirical data from the United Kingdom.
 
• According to the Phillips curve, lower unemployment in an economy is associated with higher rates of wage inflation.
 
• Conversely, higher unemployment is associated with lower rates of wage inflation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indifference Curve**

 
 
• Can be caused by **changes in consumer preferences, income levels, prices of related goods, and more**. A rightward shift indicates an increase in demand, while a leftward shift indicates a decrease.
 
• An indifference curve represents a graph showing different combinations of two goods that provide the same level of satisfaction or utility to a consumer
 
• Indicates that as a consumer consumes more of one good, they must consume less of the other to maintain the same utility level.
 
• Reflects the diminishing marginal rate of substitution; consumers are willing to give up fewer units of one good to obtain additional units of another good as they have more of it.
 
• Curves that are further from the origin represent higher levels of satisfaction.
 
 
 
• **Supply Curve**
 
 
• A supply curve illustrates the relationship between the price of a good and the quantity of that good that producers are willing to supply.
 
• Indicates that as prices increase, suppliers are willing to offer more of the good, reflecting the profit motive.
 
• Can occur due to factors such as changes in production costs, technology, or number of suppliers. A rightward shift indicates an increase in supply, while a leftward shift indicates a decrease.
 
 
 
• ** Demand Curve**
 
 
• A demand curve shows the relationship between the price of a good and the quantity demanded by consumers.
 
• Reflects the law of demand, which states that as prices decrease, the quantity demanded increases, and vice versa.
